blocks.content: Quiz: When we update an entry, why do we use map and return a new object for the edited entry instead of changing the old entry in place?
Tap an option below to answer:
React expects state updates to be immutable
Mutating state can cause bugs and missed updates. Replacing with a new array and new object lets React detect the change and re-render correctly
Mutating state can cause bugs and missed updates. Replacing with a new array and new object lets React detect the change and re-render correctly
Because map is faster than changing the old entry with a for loop
The reason is immutability, not performance.
The reason is immutability, not performance.
So we can keep the old entry in memory
We are not keeping the old entry; we are following React's rules.
We are not keeping the old entry; we are following React's rules.
So that the entry's id does not change
We keep the same id; the reason is immutable updates.
We keep the same id; the reason is immutable updates.
